cleanIntro:
The Vector 22 is a direct-blowback .22 LR rimfire Vector. It looks like the centerfire Vector and takes many of its accessories, but KRISS is plain that its upper and fire control group do not interchange with a centerfire Vector receiver, in either direction. It comes apart on its takedown pins: three let the upper assembly lift off the receiver, then two retaining pins through the spring plate free the recoil spring and bolt out of the back of the receiver. The same book covers the CRB, CRB-E, CRB Duotone, SBR and SBR-E; they differ by barrel, handguard and stock, not by procedure.

KRISS's interval is a wipe-down of the bolt and guide rails and a light oil every 400–500 rounds — more often in dust and humidity — and a complete teardown, clean and inspection at least every 1,000 rounds. Two things the book forbids: releasing the hammer while the upper is off the receiver, and removing the fire control group from the upper housing.

steps.title: Finger outside the guard, safety on
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction for the whole procedure. Take your finger out of the trigger guard and put the safety on before you do anything else.
steps.prose: Every step after this is done with hands near the action. Start from a gun that cannot fire by a slip.
steps.quote: When finished firing, ALWAYS place your finger outside the trigger guard with the barrel maintained in safe direction and activate the safety.
steps.cite: KRISS Vector 22 (CRB / SBR / CRB-E / SBR-E / CRB Duotone) — Owner's Manual — V.03_R.2023.11.06 — printed on the back page — Unloading and Clearing, printed p.11

steps.title: Magazine out first
steps.action: Press the magazine release and take the magazine out of the well.
steps.prose: Working the charging handle with a magazine still seated only chambers the next round.
steps.quote: Press the magazine release and remove the magazine.
steps.cite: KRISS Vector 22 (CRB / SBR / CRB-E / SBR-E / CRB Duotone) — Owner's Manual — V.03_R.2023.11.06 — printed on the back page — Unloading and Clearing, printed p.11

steps.title: Charging handle: turn it 90°, then pull and HOLD
steps.action: Rotate the charging handle 90 degrees and grip it as close to the receiver as you can. Pull it fully to the rear and keep holding it there — any chambered round comes out of the ejection port.
steps.prose: The handle has to be turned before it will draw the bolt back; gripping it close to the receiver keeps your hand from slipping off under the spring.
steps.quote: Rotate the charging handle 90 degrees and grip it as close to the receiver as possible. Pull and hold the charging handle to the rear.
steps.cite: KRISS Vector 22 (CRB / SBR / CRB-E / SBR-E / CRB Duotone) — Owner's Manual — V.03_R.2023.11.06 — printed on the back page — Unloading and Clearing, printed p.11

steps.title: LOOK into the chamber, then let go — and SAFE
steps.action: Still holding the handle back, look through the ejection port and see an empty chamber. Only then release the charging handle and switch the gun to Safe. Empty every round out of the magazine before it goes anywhere near the gun again.
steps.prose: Hearing a round fall out is not the check. Seeing the empty chamber is.
steps.quote: Look through the ejection port and visually confirm that the chamber is clear of ammunition. Release the charging handle.
steps.cite: KRISS Vector 22 (CRB / SBR / CRB-E / SBR-E / CRB Duotone) — Owner's Manual — V.03_R.2023.11.06 — printed on the back page — Unloading and Clearing, printed p.11

steps.title: Charge it once to reset the hammer — bolt home
steps.action: Magazine still out. Pull the charging handle back to cock the hammer, then let it go from the rear so the bolt runs fully forward into battery before any pin comes out.
steps.prose: The upper has to come off with the hammer cocked and the bolt closed; the book makes it the first step of its disassembly.
steps.caution: Check to ensure that the magazine has been removed and that chamber is cleared.
steps.quote: Pull the Charging handle back to reset the hammer. Ensure the bolt is in battery prior to step 2.
steps.cite: KRISS Vector 22 (CRB / SBR / CRB-E / SBR-E / CRB Duotone) — Owner's Manual — V.03_R.2023.11.06 — printed on the back page — Disassembly, printed p.14

steps.title: First three takedown pins out
steps.action: Push out the first three take down pins.
steps.prose: Keep the pins together — the book has you inspect all four take down pins once the gun is apart.
steps.quote: Remove the first 3 take down pins
steps.cite: KRISS Vector 22 (CRB / SBR / CRB-E / SBR-E / CRB Duotone) — Owner's Manual — V.03_R.2023.11.06 — printed on the back page — Disassembly, printed p.14

steps.title: ⚠ Upper straight up, receiver straight down
steps.action: Separate the housings by pulling the upper assembly straight up and the receiver straight down. From here until the gun is back together, do NOT let the hammer fall — no trigger pulls on the separated upper.
steps.prose: KRISS warns that dropping the hammer with the housings apart can damage the ejection port.
steps.caution: Do not release the hammer when the upper assembly has been separated from the receiver, doing so could cause damage to the ejection port.
steps.quote: Separate the housings by pulling straight up on the upper assembly and down on the receiver.
steps.cite: KRISS Vector 22 (CRB / SBR / CRB-E / SBR-E / CRB Duotone) — Owner's Manual — V.03_R.2023.11.06 — printed on the back page — Disassembly, printed p.14

steps.title: Spring plate in — two retaining pins out, left to right
steps.action: On the receiver, push the spring plate in so the two retaining pins line up, then press both retaining pins out from left to right, with a punch if you need one.
steps.prose: If a pin will not come, the plate is not lined up — push the plate in further rather than forcing the pin.
steps.quote: Press the two retaining pins out from left to right, using a punch if necessary. Do not force out the pins; they will slide out easily when correctly aligned.
steps.cite: KRISS Vector 22 (CRB / SBR / CRB-E / SBR-E / CRB Duotone) — Owner's Manual — V.03_R.2023.11.06 — printed on the back page — Disassembly, printed p.15

steps.title: Spring plate, recoil spring and bolt out the back
steps.action: Slide the spring plate, the recoil spring and the bolt out of the rear of the receiver. This is the last disassembly step the book gives.
steps.prose: Note which way up the bolt comes out — it has to go back oriented the same way.
steps.quote: Slide the spring plate, recoil spring, and bolt out of the rear of the receiver.
steps.cite: KRISS Vector 22 (CRB / SBR / CRB-E / SBR-E / CRB Duotone) — Owner's Manual — V.03_R.2023.11.06 — printed on the back page — Disassembly, printed p.15

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench: the upper assembly with the fire control group, the receiver, the bolt, the recoil spring with the guide rod and spring plate, the two retaining pins and the take down pins. That is the whole of KRISS's disassembly. DEEP CLEAN carries the book's inspection checks for the bolt face, extractor and firing pin, and its stopping point at the FCG.
steps.prose: When it goes back together, the bolt has to be the right way round and the bolt assembly complete before it goes into the receiver.
steps.quote: Ensure the bolt is oriented correctly and the bolt assembly is properly assembled before installing into the receiver.
steps.cite: KRISS Vector 22 (CRB / SBR / CRB-E / SBR-E / CRB Duotone) — Owner's Manual — V.03_R.2023.11.06 — printed on the back page — Assembly, printed p.21

deepSteps.title: Carbon under the extractor
deepSteps.action: Clean the bolt face and get the carbon out from under the extractor.
deepSteps.prose: This is the build-up the book singles out: it shows as extraction and chambering trouble before it looks bad.
deepSteps.quote: Fouling or build-up of carbon under the extractor may lead to poor extraction and poor chambering.
deepSteps.cite: KRISS Vector 22 (CRB / SBR / CRB-E / SBR-E / CRB Duotone) — Owner's Manual — V.03_R.2023.11.06 — printed on the back page — Cleaning and Inspection — Bolt, printed p.16

deepSteps.title: Extractor: cracks, chips, spring tension
deepSteps.action: Look the extractor over for cracks or chips. Then push up on its forward end — the bolt-face end — with your thumb to check the extractor spring has not weakened.
deepSteps.prose: A broken, chipped or worn extractor and a weak extractor spring are both on the book's list of causes for a failure to extract.
deepSteps.quote: Ensure that the extractor has no cracks or chips and that the extractor spring tension has not weakened.
deepSteps.cite: KRISS Vector 22 (CRB / SBR / CRB-E / SBR-E / CRB Duotone) — Owner's Manual — V.03_R.2023.11.06 — printed on the back page — Cleaning and Inspection — Bolt, printed p.16

deepSteps.title: Bolt face and firing pin
deepSteps.action: Check the bolt face for scoring or other damage and that the area round the firing pin channel is clear. Then push the firing pin from the rear with light pressure — a wooden dowel is what the book suggests — and check it moves freely and easily. Look at its tip: clear of build-up and not deformed.
deepSteps.prose: A fouled firing pin is one of the book's causes of a gun that will not fire.
deepSteps.quote: Inspect the bolt face to ensure there is no scoring or other damage. Also ensure that the area surrounding the firing pin channel is clear of build-up.
deepSteps.cite: KRISS Vector 22 (CRB / SBR / CRB-E / SBR-E / CRB Duotone) — Owner's Manual — V.03_R.2023.11.06 — printed on the back page — Cleaning and Inspection — Bolt, printed p.16

deepSteps.title: ⛔ The FCG stays in the upper — KRISS's stopping point
deepSteps.action: The fire control group in the upper housing is cleaned in place with a cotton swab or a nylon bristle brush. Do not remove it. That is as far as the book goes.
deepSteps.prose: The book says the FCG has nothing in it for an owner to service.
deepSteps.quote: Do not attempt to remove the FCG; there are no owner serviceable aspects to this assembly.
deepSteps.cite: KRISS Vector 22 (CRB / SBR / CRB-E / SBR-E / CRB Duotone) — Owner's Manual — V.03_R.2023.11.06 — printed on the back page — Cleaning and Inspection — Upper Housing, printed p.17

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Solvent-wet cotton patch in the eyelet on the bore cable; feed the cable in at the chamber and pull it all the way out of the muzzle. Repeat 2–3 times with a freshly wet patch each time.
Swap the eyelet for the brush adaptor; feed it in at the chamber and pull it through the muzzle 2–3 times.
Patches again, as the first pass, to lift the fouling the brush loosened.

cleaning.name: BOLT
tasks: Bolt face clean and free of carbon, especially under the extractor.
Area round the firing pin channel clear of build-up; firing pin tip clean.
One drop of oil on the extractor.

cleaning.name: UPPER HOUSING AND FCG
tasks: Wipe the upper housing with patches or a lint-free cloth.
Cotton swab or nylon bristle brush into the fire control group.
Ejection port mounting screws tight.
Ambidextrous fire/safe lever screws tight, with a positive click as the lever is switched back and forth.
FCG and frame tight in the housing and free of debris.

Two drops of oil on the hammer and hammer pivot pin, one on the trigger pivot pin. Thumb pressure rearward on the hammer, hold the trigger, ease the hammer forward and back again several times to spread the oil.
⛔ Never let the hammer fall freely with the upper off the receiver — it can damage the ejection port.
⛔ Do not remove the FCG from the upper housing.

cleaning.name: LOWER HOUSING AND RECEIVER
tasks: Clean it as you cleaned the upper housing.
Housing screws tight; bolt catch/release lever mounting-block screws tight.
Charging handle moves freely; its two return springs intact and clean.
Magazine release button moves freely, area underneath clear.
Ejector not loose or bent.
Two to three drops of oil in each of the left and right guide rails; thin coat of oil on the bolt raceway.
Two drops on the charging handle assembly; cycle the action to spread the oil.
Light film of oil on all metal parts before reassembly or storage, against corrosion.

cleaning.name: TAKEDOWN PINS
tasks: All four take down pins undamaged.
Clean each pin as needed.

reassembly: Check the bolt is oriented correctly and the bolt assembly is properly together before it goes in.
Slide the bolt into the rear of the receiver.
Put the recoil spring into the bolt, then press the guide rod and spring plate into the rear of the receiver.
Line the hole in the spring plate up with the front of the cutouts in the receiver and insert the two retaining pins from right to left.
Make sure the spring plate returns fully to its rearward position.
⛔ Hammer locked back before the upper goes on.
Mate the upper assembly to the receiver and replace the take down pins.
Muzzle in a safe direction — run the function check before the gun is loaded.
fncheck: Magazine OUT and the gun confirmed clear first. Charge the Vector, point it in a safe direction and pull the trigger: you should hear the hammer release and strike the firing pin. Keep the trigger held, charge the gun again, then let the trigger out slowly — there should be an audible click as it resets. Do it once more. Finally charge it, put it on Safe and try the trigger: it must be locked and the hammer must not fall. A trigger that does not reset is one of KRISS's listed faults — a weak primary sear return spring, a dirty or fouled trigger mechanism or FCG, or a damaged or broken hammer spring — and if it persists the book sends you to a KRISS Certified Dealer or KRISS USA.
